section.title: Using C++20 Modules
section.para: For projects compiled with C++20 or later, the library can be consumed through a C++20 module interface, as an alternative to including the classic headers:

The module, boost.program_options, exports the same declarations in namespace boost::program_options that are declared by the umbrella header <boost/program_options.hpp>, so existing code only needs to replace the #include with an import. A minimal, compilable example is provided in src/cppm/usage_sample.cpp.

The interface (src/cppm/boost/program_options.cppm) preloads the library's dependencies in the global module fragment and includes the umbrella header in the module purview inside an export { ... } block, so the public declarations are exported without modifying any header. The library's sources in src/*.cpp carry a BOOST_PROGRAM_OPTIONS_MODULE_UNIT conditional that compiles them, in the module build, as module implementation units providing matching module-attached definitions; in classic builds the same files compile unchanged.

section.title: Building and Using
section.para: The module interface is entirely optional. It is built by CMake when the BOOST_PROGRAM_OPTIONS_BUILD_MODULES option is enabled, producing an additional Boost::program_options_modules target which also links the classic compiled library. Building modules requires CMake 3.28 or later with the Ninja generator, or CMake 3.30 or later with the Visual Studio generator, and a compiler with C++20 modules support (MSVC 19.28+, GCC 15+, or Clang 16+). For example:

The import statement only makes the library's declarations available. As usual with modules, macros such as BOOST_PROGRAM_OPTIONS_VERSION are not exported; code that needs those macros must include the classic headers.

The standard-header includes of the library's headers and sources are wrapped in a compatibility guard following the pattern of <boost/config/std/...> from boostorg/config PR #535 (Adds support for C++20 modules): a plain #include today, and import std; in the modules mode (-DBOOST_USE_MODULES=ON, which requires a toolchain-provided std module). Once that PR is merged, the guards should be replaced with the Boost.Config headers (see the TODO comments at each guard).
